original_question: Find a combinatorial interpretation of Seidel matrices that have exactly three distinct eigenvalues.
target_in_paper: Section 3.8, Problem 3.32 of the paper: Find a combinatorial interpretation of Seidel matrices with three distinct eigenvalues. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper very closely: it names the correct object (Seidel matrices), the correct spectral condition (three distinct eigenvalues), and the correct task (to find a combinatorial interpretation), without drifting to the neighboring questions about regular graphs in a switching class or rational eigenvalues. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))
missing_details: The paper defines the Seidel matrix of a graph Γ on n vertices by S(Γ) = J_n - I_n - 2A(Γ). To make the question stand alone, that definition should be stated explicitly. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))

Equivalently, S(Γ) is the adjacency matrix of the signed complete graph on the same vertex set, with negative edges exactly the edges of Γ and positive edges exactly the nonedges; this is part of the paper’s local setup for the problem. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))

The spectral condition should be attached explicitly to S(Γ): the problem is about Seidel matrices whose real symmetric spectrum consists of exactly three distinct eigenvalues. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))

The nearby context shows the intended scope: the goal is a combinatorial interpretation for the class of such Seidel matrices, motivated by the fact that the two-eigenvalue case corresponds to regular two-graphs. That motivation is implicit in your draft. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))

Your wording should avoid importing extra hypotheses from the next problems in the paper, such as rational eigenvalues or the existence of a regular graph in the switching class; those belong to Problems 3.33 and 3.34, not Problem 3.32. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))
refined_question: Let Γ be a graph on n vertices, and let S(Γ) = J_n - I_n - 2A(Γ) denote its Seidel matrix, equivalently the adjacency matrix of the signed complete graph on the same vertex set whose negative edges are exactly the edges of Γ and whose positive edges are the nonedges. Find a combinatorial interpretation of the class of Seidel matrices S(Γ) having exactly three distinct eigenvalues. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))
justification: The draft is essentially an almost verbatim restatement of Problem 3.32 in Section 3.8. The only real omissions are the local definition of Seidel matrix and the immediate motivational context: the paper first defines S(Γ) as J_n - I_n - 2A(Γ), then notes that Seidel matrices with two distinct eigenvalues are equivalent to regular two-graphs, and only after that poses Problem 3.32 for the three-eigenvalue case. The refined version therefore keeps the original problem unchanged in scope while making the graph-theoretic setup explicit and excluding the separate follow-up questions in Problems 3.33 and 3.34. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))
